title: Release of a Completed Vehicle — Insurance Claim Repairs Repair Order Terms
content:
**Term.** A completed Insurance Claim Repairs vehicle is released to the customer only when the customer's share is settled: the repair order's customer balance is zero.

**What the customer balance contains.** The deductible, betterment, customer-pay additions and any storage are all part of that balance. The customer balance is the total of the customer charges and refunds on the repair order, less the customer's payments and the credits on it. The insurer's payment is never a condition of release.

**Evidence.** The balance is read from the repair order's own money history in the system before release; it is the record, not the customer's account of what was paid, that shows a zero balance.

**Payment.** Payment may be made by any of the class's accepted payment methods.

**Warranty.** Release issues the workmanship warranty plan the repair class sets.

## Release table

| Customer balance on the repair order | Insurer balance on the repair order | Release |
|---|---|---|
| zero | zero | released |
| zero | above zero (insurer has not paid) | released — the insurer's payment is not a condition |
| above zero | any | not released |

## Hypothetical balances

- Charges: deductible USD 500.00, betterment USD 80.00, storage USD 90.00 — USD 670.00. Payments: USD 600.00. Balance: USD 70.00. The vehicle is not released.
- The same repair order after a further card payment of USD 70.00: balance zero. The vehicle is released, and the warranty plan for its class issues, whether or not the insurer has remitted anything.
